sources.full: Icewind Dale: Rime of the Lamberto

trait.name: Snow Camouflage
entries: The hunter has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy terrain.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hunter makes two attacks, using Longbow or Shortsword in any combination.

action.name: Longbow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit +5}, range 150/600 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit +5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Piercing damage.

Tribal warriors live beyond civilization, most often subsisting on fishing and hunting. Each tribe acts in accordance with the wishes of its chief, who is the greatest or oldest warrior of the tribe or a tribe member blessed by the gods.

reaction.name: Spear the Helpless (2/Day)
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 60 feet of the hunter gains the {@condition Restrained} condition. {@actResponse} The hunter makes a ranged attack against that creature.

trait.name: Formation Tactics
entries: The soldier has Advantage on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed}, {@condition Frightened}, {@condition Grappled}, and {@condition Restrained} conditions while it is within 5 feet of at least one ally.

action.name: Spear
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit +3}, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) Piercing damage, or 6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) Slashing damage if used with two hands.

reaction.name: Backstab
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature provokes an Opportunity Attack from the soldier. {@actResponse} The soldier gives the target the {@condition Prone} condition before making a melee Spear attack against it.

trait.name: Conditioned Immunity
entries: Depending on the state of the Rune Altar, some of the Shadow's abilities are disabled:
First rune: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing immunity
Fifth rune: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}
Sixth rune: Magic Resistance

trait.name: Berserk
entries: Whenever the shadow starts its turn with 60 Hit Points or fewer, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 6, the shadow goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the shadow attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the shadow attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the shadow goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its Hit Points.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The shadow is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The shadow has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The shadow's weapon attacks are magical.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The shadow makes two Slam attacks.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a creature, {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, the target. {@actSaveFail} The target's Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the damage taken. The target dies if this reduces its Hit Point maximum to 0. The reduction lasts until removed by the {@spell greater restoration|xphb} spell or other magic.

action.name: Haste {@recharge 5}
entries: Until the end of its next turn, the shadow magically gains a +2 bonus to its AC, has Advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and can use its Slam attack as a Bonus Action.

trait.name: Frost Rune
entries: Hjoölvir has a frost rune inscribed on a chunk of ice or another object in her possession. While holding or wearing that object, she can use her Ice Wolves action and Ice Armor reaction.

The object has AC 16, 40 Hit Points, and immunity to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage. It regains all its Hit Points at the end of each of Hjoölvir's turns, but it turns to dust if reduced to 0 Hit Points or when Hjoölvir dies. If the rune is destroyed, Hjoölvir can inscribe a new one on an object in her possession when she finishes a Short Rest or Long Rest.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Hjoölvir fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Hjoölvir makes three attacks, using Greataxe or Freezing Ray in any combination.

action.name: Greataxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 10 ft. {@h}22 ({@damage 3d10 + 6}) Slashing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Cold damage.

action.name: Freezing Ray
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 10}, range 120 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 3d8 + 4}) Cold damage, and the target makes a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained} condition until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The target's Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Ice Wolves (Requires Frost Rune)
entries: Hjoölvir magically summons two wolves made of ice in unoccupied spaces she can see within 30 feet of herself. Any Ice Wolves she summoned previously disappear immediately. Each wolf has the same statistics as a {@creature winter wolf|xmm}, but it gains a +3 bonus to its attack and damage rolls while within 30 feet of Hjoölvir. The wolves take their turn immediately after Hjoölvir in the initiative order and obey her commands. The wolves disappear after 1 minute, when Hjoölvir dies, or when she uses this action again.

reaction.name: Ice Armor (Requires Frost Rune)
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature Hjoölvir can see makes an attack roll against her. {@actResponse} Hjoölvir forms a coat of ice around herself, gaining a +6 bonus to her AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss. After the attack hits or misses, the ice shatters, and each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from Hjoölvir must succeed on a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Cold damage.

Frost giants who master rune magic are known as ice shapers, and their sheer power typically contributes to a meteoric rise in the giants' ordning. Many of them end up as jarls, leading their communities, or as advisers to jarls—often the true power behind the throne. They are usually devoted to {@deity Thrym|Nonhuman|PHB}.

True to their name, these ice shapers manipulate the raw elemental energy of air and water to wield ice in both offense and defense. They summon ice elementals in the shape of wolves, cloak themselves in icy armor, and just as quickly turn that armor into a hail of deadly ice shards.

In ancient times, Hjoölvir, was well known in the Icewind Dale region, a frost giant ice shaper of immense power, able to summon ice storms with a single thought. Her throne, hidden deep in the frozen expanses of Icewind Dale, was the heart of her dominion, where two wolves of elemental fury guarded her. Fearing her growing strength, humans devised a plan to imprison her. Using mirrors that distorted light and runes that dampened her magic, they lured Hjoölvir into a trap.

The dungeon holding Hjoölvir has remained intact due to the {@adventure Twenty Stones of Thruun|IDRotF|6|Location in Dougan's Hole}, a circle of standing stones located in {@adventure Dougan's Hole|IDRotF|6}. Though these stones have held her for over a thousand years, the barrier is slowly weakening, and Hjoölvir's fury intensifies. When she breaks free, winter will descend upon the land once again.

legendary.name: Greataxe Attack
entries: Hjoölvir makes a Greataxe attack. She can't take this action again until the start of her next turn.

legendary.name: Enhanced Rush
entries: Hjoölvir moves up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

legendary.name: Absorb Elemental (Requires Frost Rune)
entries: If an Ice Wolf is within 30 feet of Hjoölvir, she magically absorbs it, regaining Hit Points equal to half the wolf's remaining Hit Points (rounded up), and the wolf disappears.

trait.name: Cold Regeneration
entries: While the temperature around him is 0°F (−18°C) or lower, Sephek regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of his turns. If Sephek takes Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on his next turn. Sephek dies only if he starts his turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

trait.name: Frozen Predator
entries: Sephek has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet in the combat.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If Sephek fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Sephek makes three attacks, using Ice Longsword or Ice Knife in any combination.

action.name: Ice Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Ice Knife
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9}, range 60 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) Piercing damage. {@hom}{@actSave dex} {@dc 17}, the target and each other creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the target. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Frostwind Slash {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, each creature in a 60-foot Cone. {@actSaveFail} 36 ({@damage 8d8}) Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

reaction.name: Frozen Riposte
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 5 feet of Sephek misses him with a melee attack. {@actResponse} Sephek makes one Ice Longsword attack against that creature.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Sephek casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

bonus.name: Whiteout Step (3/Day)
entries: Sephek teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space he can see.

legendary.name: Attack
entries: Sephek makes one Ice Longsword or Ice Knife attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Sephek moves up to his Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Sephek Kaltro is a well-built man in his thirties. He has an olive complexion, dark hair pulled back in a ponytail, and no facial or body hair. He is dressed in a stylish vest with matching pants and boots, similar in style to those worn by mariners of the southern Sword Coast, but wears no armor or cold weather clothing and doesn't appear to be armed. His most striking feature is his eyes, which are as blue as a frozen lake.

A paladin of {@deity Tempus|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, Sephek had been the caretaker of {@adventure Easthaven|IDRotF|7}'s orphanage for fifteen years. He briefly fought with the 1st Regiment in its campaign to bring down {@deity Auril|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, but had to step away to defend Easthaven before {@creature Yggdra Arlaggath|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Yggdra} rose as the town's protector.

During a journey with {@creature Adan Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Adan} and {@creature Eva Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Eva}, all three were killed by Orin Kelek, a cleric of {@deity Auril|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, who then raised them to serve both Orin himself and the Frostmaiden. Together, they will become known as the "Drow Killers," responsible for massacring multiple drow populations across {@adventure Ten-Towns|IDRotF|1} on Orin's orders.

trait.name: Aura of Winter
entries: Eva emits biting cold in a 10-foot Emanation while she isn't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}. She and her allies in that area have Resistance to Fire damage.

trait.name: Cold Regeneration
entries: While the temperature around her is 0°F (−18°C) or lower, Eva regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of her turns. If Eva takes Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on her next turn. Eva dies only if she starts her turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Eva makes two Rime Flare attacks.

action.name: Rime Flare
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) Cold damage.

action.name: Chilling Blessing (2/Day)
entries: Eva chooses up to three creatures she can see within 30 feet of herself. Each target regains 15 ({@dice 2d10 + 4}) Hit Points.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Eva casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 15}):

entries: {@creature Adan Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Adan} and Eva are slight, youthful twins with fair complexions and copper-blond hair: short and tousled in {@creature Adan Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Adan}'s case, tied back beneath a hood in Eva's. They dress alike, in blue tunics bearing the crest of {@adventure Easthaven|IDRotF|7}, fur-collared mantles, and leather bracers bound with copper cord.

{@creature Adan Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Adan} and Eva Elohim were the first orphans taken in by {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek Kaltro} when he became the caretaker of Easthaven's orphanage. Raised under his care, both regard {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek} as their father and have refused every offer of adoption, choosing to remain at the orphanage with him.

The orphanage depends on the coin {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek} earns through dangerous work, such as escorting caravans and hunting beasts that threaten {@adventure Ten-Towns|IDRotF|1}. From a young age, the twins trained to aid him in these tasks: {@creature Adan Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Adan} as a swift and relentless blade fighter, Eva as a healer devoted to the divine. Once they had proven their skill, {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek} allowed them to join him as his squires.

During a journey with {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek}, all three were killed by Orin Kelek, a cleric of {@deity Auril|Faerûnian|FRHoF}, who then raised them to serve both Orin himself and the Frostmaiden. Like {@creature Sephek Kaltro|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Sephek}, the twins are bound to Orin's will. Together, the three will become known as the "Drow Killers," responsible for massacring multiple drow populations across Ten-Towns on Orin's orders.

trait.name: Cold Regeneration
entries: While the temperature around him is 0°F (−18°C) or lower, Adan regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of his turns. If Adan takes Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on his next turn. Adan dies only if he starts his turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Adan makes three Frost Blades attacks.

action.name: Frost Blades
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) Slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Cold damage.

action.name: Glacial Dash {@recharge 5}
entries: Adan moves up to his Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. At any point during this movement, he can make one Frost Blades attack against each of up to three different creatures. Each of these attacks deals an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage on a hit, and the target's Speed is 0 until the start of Adan's next turn.

bonus.name: Icebound Agility
entries: Adan takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

Adan and {@creature Eva Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Eva} are slight, youthful twins with fair complexions and copper-blond hair: short and tousled in Adan's case, tied back beneath a hood in {@creature Eva Elohim|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Eva}'s. Together, the three will become known as the "Drow Killers," responsible for massacring multiple drow populations across Ten-Towns on Orin's orders.

trait.name: Immovable Object
entries: At the start of each of Charon's turns, if he has any Unstoppable Force charges (see below), he gains 10 Temporary Hit Points, and that number then decreases by 1.

trait.name: Unstoppable Force
entries: Charon has a number of Unstoppable Force charges (maximum 4, see Immovable Object above for how they are also spent) that increases by 1, to that maximum, each time he takes damage. Immediately after being hit by a melee attack, Charon makes an Unarmed Strike attack against the attacker; this doesn't require his reaction. Each time Charon attacks this way, the attack has an additional effect based on his current number of charges:

items.name: 1 charge.
items.entry: The target must succeed on a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet straight away from Charon.

items.name: 2 charges.
items.entry: The target must succeed on a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone} condition.

items.name: 3 charges.
items.entry: The target must succeed on a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Stunned} condition until the end of Charon's next turn.

items.name: 4 charges.
items.entry: This attack has reach 10 feet instead of 5 feet. The target must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw. {@actSaveFail} The target is reduced to 0 Hit Points. {@actSaveSuccess} The target takes 55 ({@damage 10d10}) Fire damage. Regardless of the result, Charon's charges reset to 0, and the next attack that hits him before the start of his next turn is an automatic Critical Hit.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If Charon fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Charon makes three Unarmed Strike attacks.

action.name: Unarmed Strike
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit +12}, reach 5 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 1d10 + 7}) Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wholeness of Body (1/Day)
entries: Charon regains 60 Hit Points.

reaction.name: Aura of the Guardian
entries: {@actTrigger} An attack roll hits {@creature Haumea, the 2nd Pillar|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Haumea} while Charon is within 30 feet of Haumea or of the attacker. {@actResponse} Charon teleports to a space within 5 feet of Haumea or of the attacker (whichever applies), and the triggering attack hits him instead of Haumea.

legendary.name: True Protector
entries: Charon restores his reaction.

legendary.name: Enhanced Rush
entries: Charon moves up to his Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Lightning Blood
entries: A creature within 5 feet of Haumea takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Lightning damage whenever it hits her with a melee attack that deals Piercing or Slashing damage.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries: If Haumea fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Haumea makes two attacks, using Arc Lightning or Thunderbolt in any combination.

action.name: Arc Lightning
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit +11}, reach 10 ft. or range 30 ft. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d8}) Lightning damage. If the target is a creature, it can't take reactions until the start of its next turn, and lightning jumps from the target to another creature of Haumea's choice that she can see within 30 feet of the target. The second creature must succeed on a {@dc 19} Dexterity saving throw or take 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Lightning damage.

action.name: Thunderbolt {@recharge 5}
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit +11}, range 500 ft. {@h}20 ({@damage 2d12 + 7}) Lightning damage, and the target has the {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} conditions until the start of Haumea's next turn.

bonus.name: Teleport
entries: Haumea teleports, along with any equipment she is wearing or carrying, up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that she can see.

legendary.name: Arc Lightning
entries: Haumea makes one Arc Lightning attack.

legendary.name: Protect Me!
entries: Haumea teleports {@creature Charon, the Protector|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Charon} to an unoccupied space she can see within 10 feet of herself, provided that Charon is on the same plane of existence as her. Haumea can't take this action again until the start of her next turn.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Haumea casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If the sunmaster fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Action Surge (1/Day)
entries: On her turn, the sunmaster can take one additional action.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The sunmaster makes three Lightbringer attacks.

action.name: Lightbringer
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit +9}, reach 5 ft. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is an Undead creature and Lightbringer is glowing, the sunmaster deals an extra 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Radiant damage.

action.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn (1/Day)
entries: Any magical darkness in a 30-foot Emanation originating from the sunmaster is dispelled. {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, each enemy in the emanation. {@actSaveFail} 44 ({@damage 8d10}) Radiant damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. A creature that has Total Cover from the sunmaster is unaffected.

bonus.name: Sun Strike
entries: Immediately after the sunmaster hits a creature with a weapon attack, she can trigger this Bonus Action. The target takes an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Radiant damage and ignites with radiant light. At the start of each of its turns, the ignited target takes 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Radiant damage and then makes a Constitution saving throw against {@dc 17}, ending the ignition on itself on a success. The ignition also ends after 1 minute.

reaction.name: Warding Flare (3/Day)
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature within 30 feet of the sunmaster is attacked by a creature she can see. {@actResponse} The sunmaster imposes Disadvantage on the attack roll.

legendary.name: Lightbringer
entries: The sunmaster makes one Lightbringer attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: The sunmaster moves up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The sunmaster casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

entries: Sunmasters were members of the Brotherhood of the Glorious Sun, a sect within the church of {@deity Lathander|Faerûnian|FRHoF} that believed that the Morninglord was a reincarnation of {@deity Amaunator|Faerûnian|FRHoF} and destined to transform into the Yellow God at some point in history.

Anaar is a human cleric from Marsember and sunmaster of Amaunator, she runs the {@adventure Shrine of Amaunator|IDRotF|3|Locations in Bryn Shander} located in {@adventure Bryn Shander|IDRotF|3}. When Anaar arrived to the city, she began organizing a torchbearing service, employing orphans, to light the ways of citizens moving about in the dark. Her torchbearers often brought her news of unlawful things occurring in the darkness, which she sought to deal with.

She calls Amaunator "the Morninglord," a name that southerners use to describe Lathander, a god of the dawn and rebirth. Anaar views Lathander as a usurper of Amaunator's light and doesn't like it when people confuse the two deities.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If Yggdra fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Rage (3/Day)
entries: At the start of her first turn in a fight, Yggdra enters a rage: she gains 24 ({@damage 4d8 + 6}) Temporary Hit Points, her Speed increases by 10 feet, and she has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the fight ends. Then, at the start of each of her turns while raging, she can choose another creature within 15 feet of her; that creature gains 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Temporary Hit Points.

trait.name: Relentless Rage (3/Day)
entries: If Yggdra drops to 0 Hit Points while raging and isn't killed outright, she can make a {@dc 12} Constitution Saving Throw. On a success, her Hit Points instead become 24 ({@damage 4d8 + 6}).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Yggdra makes three Ebonrose attacks.

action.name: Ebonrose
entries: While raging, Yggdra can gain Advantage on this attack roll, but attack rolls against her have Advantage until the start of her next turn. {@atkr m} {@hit +10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 2d10 + 6}) Slashing damage. If the attack misses, Yggdra can deal 5 Slashing damage to the target instead. Once per turn, Yggdra can forgo that Advantage to deal an extra 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Slashing damage and reduce the target's Speed by 15 feet until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Wither and Bloom (3/Day)
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 17}, each creature Yggdra chooses in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. Nonmagical plants in the Sphere wither. One creature in the Sphere can spend and roll up to five of its unspent Hit Dice, regaining a number of Hit Points equal to the roll plus Yggdra's Constitution modifier.

reaction.name: Branches of the Tree
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature Yggdra can see starts its turn within 30 feet of her while she is raging. {@actResponse d} {@actSave str} {@dc 18}, the triggering creature. {@actSaveFail} Spectral branches of the World Tree teleport the target to an unoccupied space Yggdra can see within 5 feet of her, or to the nearest unoccupied space she can see, and Yggdra can reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of the current turn.

legendary.name: Attack
entries: Yggdra makes one Ebonrose attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Yggdra moves up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

A half-elf barbarian of the {@subclass Path of the World Tree|Barbarian|XPHB|World Tree|XPHB}, Yggdra was raised by a nomadic tribe attuned to nature's fury. Her bond with Yggdrasil lets her channel life-giving energy and warp space to protect others. She rose to prominence during a magical blizzard that unleashed awakened ice beasts on {@adventure Easthaven|IDRotF|7}. Yggdra quelled the storm, saving the town and earning her role as Captain.

Her rigid, stoic demeanor stems from tragedy: her husband Neb, a woodcarver, and their newborn perished in an avalanche unleashed by marauding {@creature Yeti|XMM|yetis}. This tragedy fuels her tactical brilliance and quiet empathy, driving her to shield Easthaven from harm.
Yggdrasil's roots endure blizzards and bloodshed.
So shall I.

trait.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: Sabrae has Advantage on saving throws against being {@condition Charmed}, and magic can't put her to sleep.

trait.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
entries: While in sunlight, Sabrae has Disadvantage on attack rolls and on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight.

trait.name: Improved Critical
entries: Sabrae's weapon attacks score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (1/Day)
entries: If Sabrae fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Sabrae makes two Scarfall attacks.

action.name: Scarfall
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 10 ft. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 4}) Slashing damage. Hit Points lost to this attack can be restored only by a Short or Long Rest.

Once per turn on a hit, Sabrae can wound the target (maximum three Wounds at a time). At the start of its turns, a wounded creature takes {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage per Wound, then makes a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, ending all its Wounds on a success. A creature within 5 feet of it can instead take an action to make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check to end them.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Sabrae casts one of the following spells, requiring no Material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

bonus.name: Action Surge (1/Day)
entries: Sabrae takes one additional action on her turn.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: {@actTrigger} Sabrae is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon. {@actResponse} Sabrae adds 3 to her AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

legendary.name: Attack
entries: Sabrae makes one Scarfall attack.

legendary.name: Move
entries: Sabrae moves up to her Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Sabrae Lylyl is a commander of House Lylyl, a drow noble family whose soldiers answer to her without question. Disciplined and unforgiving, she leads from the front line, and her enemies learn to fear the ash-grey scars her family blade leaves behind.
She carries {@item Scarfall|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto} as both a badge of rank and a promise: House Lylyl grants the scythe only to those who can make an enemy suffer long after the battle ends.

trait.name: Malfunction
entries: Whenever Anselmo takes 15 or more damage from a single source and isn't reduced to 0 Hit Points by it, roll a {@dice d20} to determine whether it suffers a malfunction:

items.name: 11–12: "My Mind Is Going. I Can Feel It."
items.entry: Anselmo has the {@condition Incapacitated} condition for 1 minute.

items.name: 13–14: "You've Disarmed Me!"
items.entry: One of Anselmo's arms falls off, reducing the number of Shock attacks it makes with Multiattack by 1 until a creature takes the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to reattach the arm.

items.name: 15–16: "Who Turned Out the Lights?"
items.entry: Anselmo's head falls off and deactivates. Anselmo has the {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Deafened} conditions until a creature takes the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to reattach the head.

items.name: 17–20: "Have a Magical Day!"
items.entry: Anselmo explodes and is destroyed. {@actSave dex} {@dc 11}, each creature in a 20-foot Emanation originating from Anselmo. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Slashing damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

trait.name: Mechanical Nature
entries: If the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell is cast on Anselmo, it regains 7 ({@dice 2d6}) Hit Points. If Anselmo has died within the last hour, a creature can revive it by using {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} and expending a spell slot of level 1 or higher.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Anselmo makes two Shock attacks.

action.name: Shock
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) Lightning damage.
Anselmo is a mechagnome made thousands of years ago to aid Netherese arcanists with their daily tasks.
Regardless of what its insides are made of, it has a metallic outer casing painted with gnomish features. It walks with a stiff gait, clanking, wheezing, whirring, and buzzing wherever it goes.

A mechagnome obeys its creator's commands when it is functioning properly, but a design flaw can cause a mechagnome to go rogue, forget its orders, and wander doing anything except what it was designed for.
Anselmo specifically was made by Drakareth, a powerful human archmage who ruled over one of the many towers of {@adventure Ythryn|IDRotF|17}.

Its original purpose was to aid any guests of the tower in any of their necessities, but due to the course of time and the ambiguous nature of the command, the mechagnome doesn't discern the intentions of anyone, offering its help to any new visitor who enters the {@adventure upside-down tower ruins|IDRotF|12|Lost Spire of Netheril}.
It has knowledge of every room of the tower and will doubtlessly help its guests find the remaining secrets in the ruins, if asked the right questions.

trait.name: Drunken Antimagic Cone
entries: Elta's central eye emits an antimagic wave in a 150-foot Cone that works like the {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB} spell, even against Elta's own Eye Rays. At the start of each of its turns, Elta decides which way the Cone faces and whether it is active, then makes a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, Elta is too dizzy to focus its eye, and the Cone is inactive until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Onion Stench
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, any creature that starts its turn in a 5-foot Emanation originating from Elta. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Poisoned} condition until the start of its next turn, overcome by an irremediable feeling of nausea. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to this Onion Stench for 24 hours.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 3}, reach 5 ft. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Poison damage from sheer alcohol poisoning.

action.name: Eye Rays
entries: Elta shoots two different "magical" eye rays at random (roll {@dice 1d4} twice, rerolling duplicates), choosing one or two targets it can blurrily see within 90 feet of itself. Its other eyestalks are busy holding beers.

items.name: 1: Confusion Ray
items.entry: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15}, one creature. {@actSaveFail} The target sees the world through the eyes of a drunk until the end of its next turn. It can't move, and it uses its action to make a melee attack against a random creature within its reach, even one of its mates. If it can't attack anyone, it spends its action yelling insults at the sky.

items.name: 2: Paralyzing Ray
items.entry: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, one creature. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Paralyzed} condition and repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. Meanwhile, it drools everywhere and people paint dicks on its forehead.

items.name: 3: Slowing Ray
items.entry: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, one creature. {@actSaveFail} The target gets drunk for 1 minute. While drunk, its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and it can take either an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, sobering up on a success.

items.name: 4: Wounding Ray
items.entry: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, one creature. {@actSaveFail} 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage. This is an accurate simulation of what's happening to Elta's liver.

entries: The stench of stale ale drifts up from the cellar, chipped pint glasses clink together, and a single glazed, rheumy eye lights up the darkness. Relax: the beerholder just wants to be your friend. Or to kill you. Or to tell you a long, pointless story and borrow a few coins. Probably all three, in that order.

entries.name: Appearance
entries: Decades of neglect, self-abuse, and bad decisions have turned the beerholder into a giant floating sack of flesh with a pint in every eyestalk. It smells like your uncle.

entries.name: Arrogance
entries: Constant drink fills a beerholder with bravado. It boasts loudly about its achievements, usually in the third person, while hovering around doing nothing at all. It bullies lesser creatures into fetching its beer.

entries.name: Cellar Dweller
entries: Beerholders are drawn to cellars, breweries, and the back rooms of taverns. When the booze runs out, they slump onto the nearest couch and piss and moan until someone brings more.

entries.name: Elta's Tavern
entries: Elta Bernero has turned the vice into a business. It runs a tavern on a small plane of its own, where there are no windows, no clocks, and time flows differently. Patrons who drop in "for just one drink" often stumble out to find days have passed outside. Elta insists this is not its fault. It is still early, it says, every time anyone asks.
The tavern has no fixed address. Once a week, doors to Elta's tavern appear along the Sword Coast, and anyone who walks through one ends up at the bar.
The tavern is warped by Elta's presence, which creates the following effects:

items.name: Weekly Doors
items.entry: One day each week, plain wooden doors marked with a painted tankard appear in cellars, alleys, and inn walls along the Sword Coast. Any creature that passes through one arrives at the tavern. The doors vanish at dawn.

items.name: Time Flies
items.entry: For every hour a creature spends inside the tavern, {@dice 1d6} hours pass in the outside world.

items.name: Last-Call Blizzard
items.entry: Doors don't last long in Icewind Dale, so the tavern finds its patrons another way. Once a week, a magical blizzard rises somewhere in the region. Any creature caught in it is teleported to the tavern.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Copper makes three attacks, using Scratch or Hand Crossbow in any combination. He can replace one attack with a Bite attack.

action.name: Bite (Rat or Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. {@actSave con} {@dc 13}. {@actSaveFail} The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it instead becomes a {@creature Wererat|XMM} under the DM's control and has 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is immune to Copper's curse for 24 hours.

action.name: Scratch
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Hand Crossbow (Humanoid or Hybrid Form Only)
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 7}, range 30/120 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Piercing damage.

action.name: Rat Swarm {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point Copper can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 17 ({@damage 5d6}) Piercing damage, and the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

bonus.name: Nimble Escape
entries: Copper takes the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} action.

bonus.name: Shape-Shift
entries: Copper shape-shifts into a Small rat-humanoid hybrid or a Tiny rat, or he returns to his true gnome form. His game statistics, other than his size, are the same in each form. Any equipment he is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

Copper Knobberknocker is a rock gnome {@creature Wererat|XMM|wererat} who lives in the attic of the {@adventure Shrine of Amaunator|IDRotF|3|Locations in Bryn Shander} in {@adventure Bryn Shander|IDRotF|3}, where he begrudgingly helps with services and chores.

{@creature Anaar (Sunmaster)|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto|Anaar} and he argue incessantly about the true identity of the Morninglord: Copper defends {@deity Lathander|Faerûnian|FRHoF} as the real incarnation of the deity, while Anaar defends her beliefs in {@deity Amaunator|Faerûnian|FRHoF}.
Copper walks around in a fuzzy suit and hood that he made himself; although it's quite warm, it makes him look like a teddy bear.

item.name: Ebonrose
item.reqAttune: by a follower of the Path of the World Tree

entries.name: Wither and Bloom (3/Day)
entries: Ebonrose lets its bearer channel the World Tree's power. You can use an action to cast {@spell wither and bloom|scc} from Ebonrose as a 6th-level spell (spell save DC 17), requiring no material components. You can use this property a total of three times, and Ebonrose regains all expended uses at dawn.

Ebonrose is a glaive whose haft is a living branch grafted from Yggdrasil itself, its head unfurling in thorned black petals like a rose in eternal bloom. It was given to {@creature Yggdra Arlaggath|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto} by the World Tree in recognition of her unbroken vigil over {@adventure Easthaven|IDRotF|7}.

The weapon answers fully only to a bearer whose fury is tempered by devotion to something greater than themselves; in less devoted hands it still functions as a fine magic glaive, but none of the tales told of it are theirs to claim.

item.name: Scarfall
entries: Hit Points a creature loses to damage from Scarfall can be restored only by finishing a Short or Long Rest.

Once per turn on a hit, you can wound the target (maximum three Wounds at a time). At the start of its turns, a wounded creature takes 1d4 Necrotic damage per Wound, then makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, ending all its Wounds on a success. A creature within 5 feet of it can instead take an action to make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check to end them.

Scarfall is a drow scythe forged in the Lylyl family's ancestral halls, its blackened blade said to leave wounds that scar over ash-grey and never quite heal clean, like snow that falls and never fully melts.

House Lylyl grants the weapon only to commanders who have proven they can make an enemy suffer long after the battle ends. {@creature Sabrae Lylyl|IcewindDaleRimeoftheLamberto} carries it as both a badge of rank and a promise: those who survive its first cut rarely walk away whole.
